subject: Archaeology
title: Muon Tomography: X-Raying Pyramids
description: A micro-lesson that makes Muon Tomography: X-Raying Pyramids usable.

hook.text: Cosmic rays through the Great Pyramid revealed a hidden void 100 feet long.

buildup.text: Muons are subatomic particles from space. Dense stone absorbs more muons than empty air.

discovery.text: The ScanPyramids project placed detectors inside. A void above the Grand Gallery appeared.

twist.text: No one knows what the void holds or if it is structural. Drilling risks damage.

climax.text: Tiny robots may enter through micro-drilled holes. The technology is being developed now.

punchline.text: Cosmic rays found a secret room. We still cannot get inside.

quiz.question: How did scientists find the hidden void in the Great Pyramid?
options: Muon detectors measured cosmic ray absorption — voids absorb fewer muons

details.summary: Muon tomography uses naturally occurring cosmic ray particles that penetrate stone to detect voids inside massive structures. The ScanPyramids project used this technique to discover a large hidden chamber inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in 2017 — the first new internal space found since the 1800s.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional excavation cannot probe sealed stone structures without damage. Muon tomography offers a completely non-invasive way to see inside pyramids, temples, and other massive buildings that have never been opened.
takeaways: Muon tomography detects voids inside massive stone structures
It discovered a hidden chamber in the Great Pyramid in 2017
The technique is completely non-invasive and non-destructive

faq.question: How does muon tomography work?
faq.answer: Cosmic rays produce muons that pass through solid matter. Detectors placed inside or beneath a structure measure muon density. Air-filled voids allow more muons through than solid stone, creating density maps that reveal hidden chambers without drilling a single hole.

faq.question: What was found inside the Great Pyramid using muon tomography?
faq.answer: The ScanPyramids project detected a large void at least 30 meters long above the Grand Gallery. Its purpose remains unknown — it could be a construction feature, a relieving chamber, or a sealed room. Non-invasive exploration methods are being developed to investigate further.
